Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot scope: EU/APAC fit checks & prompt pack request

Hi Anna —

Great to speak yesterday. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we can lock the pilot scope:

Summary of ask (what LinguaTech needs):
- Verify model fit for consumer-facing assistant UX across EU languages (en, de, fr, es, nl) and APAC (ja, ko, zh-Hans).
- Measure quality regressions against your existing rule-based fallback for edge cases (privacy/legal queries + monetary amounts).
- Deliver a prompt set and baseline benchmarks so your engineers can validate integration performance.

Our recommended pilot outline (2 weeks):
1) Model shortlist & profiles: Mistral-7B-instruct (8-bit), Llama-3-13B-ptq, Redstone-7B-quant (our internal quant candidate) — run classification/QA-style prompt bundle.
2) Evaluation suite: 10k utterances sampled across locales (proportionally weighted to traffic you quoted: DE 20%, FR 15%, ES 10%, NL 5%, EN 20%, JA 15%, KO 10%, ZH 5%). Metrics: semantic similarity (embedding cosine), human rating (3-point acceptability), hallucination rate, latency p95.
3) Prompt pack: initial set (~160 prompts) covering greetings, policy-sensitive queries, numeric extraction, and locale-specific politeness variants.
4) Deliverables: CSV prompt set, PDF benchmark summary, SOW draft for next phase.

Open questions we flagged for the SOW:
- Data residency: you mentioned EU-only audit logs for production — confirm whether pilot needs EU-hosted runtime.
- Languages to prioritize for manual annotation (you suggested DE/JA).
- Any blacklisted content categories we should exclude from synthetic prompt generation.

I've attached a starter prompt_sets_v1.csv and a short benchmark_results_summary.pdf with model microbenchmarks. Can Neha/Marissa weigh in on the scoring thresholds we should use for go/no-go?

Proposed next meeting: 30-min sync Thu 09/23 10:00-10:30 PT to finalize SOW + pilot cadence. If that works for you we’ll send a calendar invite and SOW v2.

Thanks —
Ben

Adding model-fit guidance and threshold proposals.

Ben / Anna —

Quick notes from the evaluation team (actionable stuff you can include in SOW):
- Candidate models and why:
  * Mistral-7B-instruct (8-bit): strong instruction-following in Romance languages, low latency; risk: occasional verbosity on policy answers.
  * Llama-3-13B-ptq: better on factual recall in EN/DE, heavier memory but acceptable p95 if we tune batching.
  * Redstone-7B-quant: our quant baseline with aggressive memory footprint; good for on-prem/Dedicated tests.

- Suggested scoring thresholds (pilot pass):
  * Human acceptability >= 75% across sampled dialogs per locale.
  * Hallucination rate <= 6% on policy/legal prompts (human-audited).
  * Embedding cosine (vs. ground-truth answer) >= 0.78 average.
  * Latency p95 <= 450ms (EU-hosted infra target).

- Prompt-pack notes: we expanded locale variants to include formal/informal German (Sie/du) and honorific forms in Japanese (san/kun) for the 20 canonical intents. See prompt_sets_v1.csv: column 'locale_variant' + 'jurisdiction_sensitive'.

Attachments included: prompt_sets_v1.csv (seed prompts), benchmark_results_summary.pdf (per-model microbench). I've updated the Drive folder with a working evaluation script (link below).

Proposed pilot tasks and owners:
- Redwood: run model candidate microbenchmarks + produce benchmark_results_summary.pdf (Neha).
- LinguaTech: provide seed authoritative queries + priority language list (Anna).
- LinguaTech + Redwood: 3-way review of failed examples after 1st run, then manual annotation for DE/JA (Marissa to own annotation plan).

Couple of operational notes from QA readiness perspective before we kick off: 

- Japanese-specific: please include normalization rules for full-width/half-width digits and address variations (kanji vs kana). We'll need an extra pass for numeric extraction tests.
- German formal vs informal: sample sets should explicitly mark desired register per example — otherwise model scoring will be noisy.
- Annotation tip: use a 3-level rubric (Pass / Needs Edit / Fail) with a short rationale field to speed adjudication.

If Anna can confirm seed upload, Marissa will schedule two 90-min annotation sessions in week 1 and provide an interim report after run 1.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Localization Engineer, Redwood Inference
